input.question: Why does Rogaine only work for the top of your head, but not for your receding hairline?
input.ground_truth: From what I understand, Rogaine *can* work anywhere it's applied. It's a marketing move that says only use on your vertex. Reason, its a harder area for a guy to inspect. You can use it on your hairline, they just won't say you can. Source, My mom's friend is a dermatologist. She (the dermatologist) and her sisters got *really* lucky and managed to get the genes for baldness on both X chromosomes (and whatever related chromosomes needed for women to go bald). Her sisters wear wigs. She has beed using "Men's" Rogaine for many years. She still has a full, although thin for a woman, head of hair. Obilgatory side fact - We don't know exactly how Mydoxinal (Rogaine) works. But it does. DO NOT QUESTION THE MAGIC.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why does Rogaine only work for the top of your head, but not for your receding hairline?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your hair is like a garden. Rogaine is like special food that helps hair grow, but it only works where the soil (your scalp) still has the seeds (hair follicles) to help grow new hair.

If your hairline is receding, it means the seeds are gone from that part of the garden. So, even if you put the special food (Rogaine) there, nothing will grow because there are no seeds left.

But on the top of your head, if there are still seeds (hair follicles), the special food can help them grow hair again! That’s why Rogaine works on the top, but not on a receding hairline.
